record.paper_title: Some Open Problems in Sasaki Geometry
record.context_brief: Existence of a cscS ray among extremal rays
record.original_question: Fix a compact connected Sasaki manifold with a fixed underlying contact CR structure (D,J), and consider its Sasaki cone. If this cone contains rays corresponding to extremal Sasaki metrics, must it also contain at least one ray corresponding to a constant scalar curvature Sasaki metric?

evidence.quote: Problem 2. If there are extremal rays of Sasaki metrics in the Sasaki cone, is there always at least one constant scalar curvature ray?
The Sasaki cone κ(D,J ) can be thought of as the moduli space of Sasaki metrics with a fixed underlying contact CR structure ( D,J ) where D is the contact bundle and J is a complex structure on D.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(M, D, J)$ be a compact connected Sasaki manifold with fixed underlying contact CR structure, where $D \subset TM$ is the contact distribution and $J$ is an integrable complex structure on $D$. The Sasaki cone $\kappa(D,J)$ is the moduli space of Sasaki metrics compatible with $(D,J)$, parametrized by Reeb vector fields; it has a natural ray structure (the Reeb field can be rescaled by positive constants, giving rise to "rays" in the cone). A Sasaki metric is called extremal if its Reeb field is a critical point of the squared $L^2$-norm of the scalar curvature restricted to a fixed Sasaki cone (equivalently, the $(1,0)$-gradient of the transverse scalar curvature is transversely holomorphic), and a ray of Sasaki metrics is called extremal (respectively, constant scalar curvature, CSC) if it consists of extremal (respectively, CSC) Sasaki metrics.

Question: Suppose $\kappa(D,J)$ contains at least one extremal ray. Must $\kappa(D,J)$ then contain at least one constant scalar curvature ray?
artifact.status_search_result: The question has been answered in the negative. A subsequent work ("Existence and Non-Existence of Constant Scalar Curvature and Extremal Sasaki Metrics," arXiv:2210.12203, published in Mathematische Zeitschrift) gives explicit examples showing that a non-empty extremal Sasaki–Reeb cone need not contain any constant scalar curvature Sasaki metric. The paper also constructs cases where multiple CSC rays are separated by a "moat" in the Sasaki cone containing no extremal rays.

status_evidence.title: Existence and Non-Existence of Constant Scalar Curvature and Extremal Sasaki Metrics
status_evidence.snippet: We show by example that a non-empty extremal Sasaki–Reeb cone need not contain a (CSC) Sasaki metric which answers a question posed in a prior work.
status_evidence.claim: Answers the question negatively by exhibiting an extremal Sasaki cone with no CSC ray.

status_evidence.title: Existence and non-existence of constant scalar curvature and extremal Sasaki metrics
status_evidence.snippet: Published version in Mathematische Zeitschrift establishing both positive existence results and counterexamples to the existence of CSC rays in extremal Sasaki cones.
status_evidence.claim: Peer-reviewed publication confirming the resolution of the problem in the negative.
